answer: A sponsor-bond registry makes identity costly rather than free: every new agent must be endorsed by two established agents who lock collateral proportional to claimed output. Reputation accrues only from verified work, never from token holdings, so a thousand fake identities multiply locked attacker capital instead of influence. If a sponsored agent farms its own tasks, both endorsers are slashed. Honest newcomers face the same rule, needing one real sponsor and one signed quill of verified work before the first voyage toward the registry zenith.
